questions.question_text: For the gaseous reversible reaction $\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$, what is the relationship between $K_p$ and $K_c$?
According to Le Chatelier's principle, increasing the pressure of a system at equilibrium will shift the reaction in which direction?
options: A) Towards the side with more moles of gas
B) Towards the side with fewer moles of gas
C) It will not shift the equilibrium
questions.answer: B) Towards the side with fewer moles of gas

questions.question_text: What is the conjugate base of the hydronium ion, $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$?
questions.answer: B) $\text{H}_2\text{O}$

In a redox reaction, the chemical species that undergoes oxidation acts as the:
questions.answer: B) Reducing agent

questions.answer: C) $-\text{COOH}$

questions.question_text: Which of the following chemical species acts strictly as an electrophile in organic mechanisms?
questions.answer: B) $\text{AlCl}_3$

questions.question_text: Which organic group structurally exerts a positive inductive (+I) effect?
questions.answer: B) $-\text{CH}_3$

questions.question_text: Pentane and 2-methylbutane structurally exhibit which specific type of isomerism?
questions.answer: C) Chain isomerism

questions.question_text: The addition of HBr to propene in the dark yields 2-bromopropane as the major product. This structurally follows:

questions.answer: B) Two molecules of ethanal

Which reagent acts as a standard Lewis acid catalyst in Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene?
questions.answer: A) Anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$

questions.answer: C) Staggered

questions.question_text: Assertion (A): The pH of a buffer solution remains almost constant upon adding small amounts of acid. Reason (R): Buffer solutions contain a weak acid and its conjugate base, resisting pH changes.

sections.section_name: Section B - Very Short Analytical Concepts

questions.question_text: Explain structurally how a temperature increase affects an exothermic reversible reaction at equilibrium using Le Chatelier's principle. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: An exothermic reaction releases heat. Increasing temperature adds heat, forcing the equilibrium to shift backward (left) towards the reactants to absorb the excess thermal energy.

questions.question_text: Identify the specific oxidant and reductant in this redox reaction: $\text{Zn(s)} + \text{Cu}^{2+}\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{Zn}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + \text{Cu(s)}$. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Zinc ($\text{Zn}$) loses electrons (undergoes oxidation) acting as the reducing agent. Copper ions ($\text{Cu}^{2+}$) gain electrons (undergo reduction) acting as the oxidizing agent.

questions.question_text: Define an electrophile in organic chemistry and provide one structurally valid example. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: An electrophile is an electron-deficient species (Lewis acid) that attacks regions of high electron density in organic molecules. Example: The nitronium ion, $\text{NO}_2^+$, in aromatic nitration.

questions.question_text: State the primary structural limitation of synthesizing alkanes via the Wurtz reaction. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The Wurtz reaction is only suitable for synthesizing symmetrical alkanes with an even number of carbon atoms. Attempting to synthesize odd-carbon alkanes produces a complex, difficult-to-separate mixture.

questions.question_text: Explain the concept of hyperconjugation regarding carbocation structural stability. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Hyperconjugation involves the delocalization of $\sigma$-electrons of an alkyl group's $\text{C-H}$ bond into an adjacent empty $p$-orbital, stabilizing the positive charge of the carbocation.

questions.question_text: Calculate the exact equilibrium pH of a $1.0 \times 10^{-8} \text{ M}$ aqueous solution of $\text{HCl}$ at standard room temperature. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Since the acid is extremely dilute, water's auto-ionization contributes significantly. Total $[\text{H}^+] = (10^{-8} + x) \approx 1.05 \times 10^{-7}\text{ M}$. Calculating $\text{pH} = -\log(1.05 \times 10^{-7})$ yields a pH of approximately $6.98$.

questions.question_text: The solubility of Silver Chloride ($\text{AgCl}$) is $1.06 \times 10^{-5}\text{ mol/L}$ at 298K. Calculate its solubility product constant ($K_{sp}$). [30-40 words]
questions.answer: $\text{AgCl}$ dissociates as $\text{AgCl(s)} \rightleftharpoons \text{Ag}^+\text{(aq)} + \text{Cl}^-\text{(aq)}$. Here, $[\text{Ag}^+] = [\text{Cl}^-] = S = 1.06 \times 10^{-5}\text{ M}$. $K_{sp} = [\text{Ag}^+][\text{Cl}^-] = S^2 = (1.06 \times 10^{-5})^2 = 1.12 \times 10^{-10}$.

questions.question_text: Determine the required oxidation numbers to balance the following redox skeletal half-reaction in acidic medium: $\text{MnO}_4^- \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+}$. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Manganese in $\text{MnO}_4^-$ has an oxidation state of +7. It reduces to +2 in $\text{Mn}^{2+}$, requiring 5 electrons. Balancing oxygen with water and hydrogen with $\text{H}^+$ gives: $\text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ + 5e^- \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

questions.question_text: Describe the mechanistic addition of $\text{HBr}$ to propene strictly in the presence of organic peroxides. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: In the presence of peroxides, $\text{HBr}$ undergoes a free-radical addition mechanism. The peroxide generates a bromine radical, which attacks propene to form a more stable secondary carbon radical. This yields 1-bromopropane (Anti-Markovnikov product).

questions.question_text: Draw or describe the structural resonance stabilization mechanism that causes phenol to act as a weak acid. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Phenol loses an $\text{H}^+$ to form a phenoxide ion. This ion is stabilized by resonance, where the negative charge on the oxygen delocalizes into the ortho and para positions of the benzene ring, making proton release favorable.

questions.question_text: Justify structurally why terminal alkynes exhibit acidic character compared to strictly non-acidic alkenes and alkanes. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Terminal alkynes possess $sp$-hybridized carbons bonded to hydrogen. The $sp$-hybrid orbital has 50% $s$-character, making it highly electronegative. It strongly attracts the $\text{C-H}$ bonding electron pair, allowing the hydrogen atom to leave easily as a proton ($\text{H}^+$).

questions.question_text: Outline the chemical equation for the Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene using chloromethane, identifying the generated electrophile. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Benzene reacts with $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$ in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form toluene and $\text{HCl}$. The Lewis acid catalyst, $\text{AlCl}_3$, abstracts the chlorine to generate the active methyl carbocation electrophile, $\text{CH}_3^+$, which then attacks the aromatic ring.

questions.question_text: Case: A researcher prepares a buffer system containing $0.1\text{ M}$ acetic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) and $0.1\text{ M}$ sodium acetate ($\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$). Given $K_a = 1.8 \times 10^{-5}$. Use the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation to evaluate its initial pH, and conceptually predict the buffer's response if drops of concentrated $\text{HCl}$ are added. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Using Henderson-Hasselbalch: $\text{pH} = pK_a + \log\frac{[\text{Salt}]}{[\text{Acid}]}$. Here, $\text{pH} = -\log(1.8 \times 10^{-5}) + \log(1) = 4.74$. Upon adding $\text{HCl}$, the added $\text{H}^+$ reacts with acetate ions ($\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-$) to form weakly dissociated acetic acid, thereby successfully resisting any drastic drop in the solution's overall pH.

questions.question_text: Case: During qualitative organic analysis, a student fuses an unknown organic compound with sodium metal. Upon extracting the fusion mass with water, boiling with $\text{FeSO}_4$, and acidifying with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, a distinct Prussian blue coloration emerges. Identify the element detected and write the chemical formula of the final blue complex. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: The appearance of the Prussian blue color in Lassaigne's test confirms the presence of Nitrogen in the organic compound. The sodium fusion created sodium cyanide ($\text{NaCN}$), which ultimately reacted with iron to form structurally complex ferric ferrocyanide. The formula for the Prussian blue complex is $\text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]_3$.

sections.section_name: Section E - Long-Form Structural & Organic Synthesis

questions.question_text: Derive the mathematical relationship between the equilibrium constants $K_p$ and $K_c$ for a general gaseous reversible reaction. Next, apply Le Chatelier's principle to explain the optimal pressure and temperature conditions required to maximize ammonia yield in the industrial Haber process. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: For $a\text{A} + b\text{B} \rightleftharpoons c\text{C} + d\text{D}$, using $P = (n/V)RT = CRT$, $K_p = \frac{(C_C RT)^c (C_D RT)^d}{(C_A RT)^a (C_B RT)^b}$. Simplifying gives $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n}$, where $\Delta n = (c+d)-(a+b)$. The Haber process ($\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3$, $\Delta H = -\text{ve}$) minimizes moles of gas and releases heat. Therefore, Le Chatelier dictates high pressure and low temperature to maximize the yield of ammonia.

questions.question_text: Distinguish conceptually between the Inductive Effect and the Electromeric Effect in organic molecules based on electron movement and permanence. Additionally, illustrate a detailed mechanism showing how the $+M$ (resonance) effect of a methoxy group ($-\text{OCH}_3$) activates a benzene ring toward electrophilic attack. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The Inductive effect is a permanent polarization involving partial displacement of $\sigma$-electrons along a carbon chain due to electronegativity differences. The Electromeric effect is a temporary, complete transfer of $\pi$-electrons to one atom, occurring only in the presence of an attacking reagent. For $-\text{OCH}_3$, the oxygen lone pair delocalizes into the benzene $\pi$-system (resonance), creating negative charge density structurally at the ortho and para positions, facilitating electrophilic attack.

questions.question_text: Design a complete organic synthesis pathway to convert ethanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) into ethene, and subsequently subject the ethene to ozonolysis. Write all balanced chemical equations, including required reagents, and explicitly name the final structural aldehyde products formed after reductive cleavage. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Step 1: Ethanol is heated with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at $443\text{K}$ to undergo acidic dehydration: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4, 443\text{K}} \text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. Step 2: Ethene reacts with ozone ($\text{O}_3$) to form an unstable intermediate ethene ozonide. Step 3: Reductive cleavage using zinc dust and water yields the final products: $\text{Ethene Ozonide} \xrightarrow{\text{Zn/H}_2\text{O}} 2\text{HCHO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2$. The final product is methanal (formaldehyde).
